biography: Hubert Haupt, a name synonymous with audacious overtakes and unwavering aggression on the track, hails from a small Bavarian town where the roar of engines was as common as church bells. His racing journey began not on asphalt, but on snow-covered fields, tearing around on a modified go-kart his father, a local mechanic, had built. This early experience instilled in him a raw, intuitive understanding of vehicle dynamics. Haupt's defining moment came during the 1998 DTM season at the Norisring, where, against all odds, he wrestled his Audi V8 quattro to victory, a testament to his sheer willpower and car control. Now, at 33, Haupt remains a force to be reckoned with in the Audi V8 quattro DTM series, his relentless pursuit of victory undiminished.
drivingStyle: Haupt's driving style is best described as 'controlled aggression'. He's known for late-braking maneuvers and an uncanny ability to find grip where others can't. Tire management isn't exactly his forte; he prefers to extract maximum performance early in a stint, often pushing the rubber to its limit. Under pressure, Haupt thrives, transforming into an even more formidable opponent, relishing the challenge of wheel-to-wheel combat.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from a controversial collision in the 2000 Hockenheim race, where Haupt's aggressive move sent Richter spinning out of contention.

A battle of egos and talent, as Haupt and Schnell are often neck-and-neck on the track, pushing each other to the absolute limit. Their contrasting driving styles frequently lead to thrilling on-track duels.
Weber constantly accuses Haupt of unsportsmanlike conduct, claiming his aggressive tactics border on dangerous. The two have exchanged heated words both on and off the track.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky driving gloves, rumored to have been his father's.
Listens to classical music (Wagner) to calm his nerves before each race.
Refuses to shave on race days, believing it jinxes his chances.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. I race to win, and I'll do whatever it takes to get there."
careerHighlight: Winning the 1998 DTM race at the Norisring after starting from the back of the grid, showcasing his raw talent and determination.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 1999 Nürburgring race due to a mechanical failure, costing him a certain victory.
